question: What is the main focus of the primary health care tier in Nigeria?
explanation: You've got this! The primary tier is right at the grassroots, focusing on keeping communities healthy and stopping illnesses early before they get worse. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which tier of Nigeria's healthcare system acts as the first place patients are referred to from primary clinics?
explanation: Spot on! Secondary health care uses general hospitals to handle cases that need more attention than a primary health center can manage. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h1)

question: Who usually sets up tertiary health facilities in Nigeria?
explanation: Great job! While some states own teaching hospitals too, the federal government establishes the majority of these big tertiary institutions. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h2)

question: What are the three main duties of tertiary health centers in Nigeria?

options.A: Revenue generation, drug manufacturing, and politics
options.B: Road safety, nutrition, and maternal education
options.C: Specialized clinical care, training, and research

explanation: Think of teaching hospitals: they treat complex patients, train student doctors and midwives, and carry out medical research to find better treatments! [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h2)

question: In a hospital, what does the abbreviation NICU stand for?
explanation: You'll see this wonderful unit a lot during your postings! The NICU is where premature or very sick newborn babies get round-the-clock specialized care. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h3)

question: Where is the best place to care for a pregnant woman with severe pre-eclampsia and failing kidneys?
explanation: When complications get this serious, a tertiary hospital is needed because they have the advanced specialists and equipment to handle multiple failing organs. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the title of the boss who runs a Federal Teaching Hospital in Nigeria?
explanation: The Chief Medical Director (CMD) is the one in charge of the everyday executive management of a federal teaching hospital. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the main job of the Director of Nursing Services in a big hospital?

options.A: Conducting external financial audits for the federal government
options.B: Appointing members of the hospital board of management
options.C: Purchasing hospital drugs and medical equipment
options.D: Overseeing professional nursing standards and clinical staffing

explanation: As future midwives, you'll love this: the DNS looks after the nursing workforce, keeps patient care standards high, and speaks up for the nursing team. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is a big problem affecting how patients move through referral steps to tertiary hospitals?

options.A: Tertiary hospitals only accept patients via postal mail
options.B: Patients frequently bypass lower tiers through direct self-referral
options.C: Secondary hospitals lack basic transportation for staff
options.D: Primary clinics refuse to refer any obstetric cases at all

explanation: Many people go straight to teaching hospitals even for minor issues, which causes massive overcrowding and makes it harder to treat true emergencies. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which health center is usually the first stop when a patient is referred away from community care?
explanation: You got it! Secondary hospitals receive patients coming from primary health centers before deciding if an even higher level of care is needed. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h5)

question: Aside from caring for patients, what is another major duty of tertiary health institutions?

options.B: Issuing national birth and death certificates
options.C: Training health professionals and conducting research

explanation: Teaching hospitals do double duty: they look after sick patients while also shaping the minds of future health workers and discovering new medical solutions. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h6)

question: How do maternal mortality reviews in tertiary hospitals help the rest of the health system?

options.A: By identifying preventable causes of death to improve future care policies
options.B: By increasing the financial revenue generated by the hospital
options.C: By reducing the total number of patients seeking antenatal care
options.D: By punishing healthcare workers who make clinical mistakes

explanation: Reviewing tough cases isn't about blaming anyone—it's about learning what went wrong so we can protect mothers better across all clinics and hospitals. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h6)

question: What does the term 'brain drain' mean in the Nigerian health sector?

options.A: Loss of medical records due to poor computer database systems
options.B: Emigration of skilled healthcare professionals to other countries
options.C: Mental fatigue caused by long working hours in emergency wards
options.D: Decline in patient cognitive assessments during geriatric care

explanation: It's a big topic of discussion today: 'brain drain' happens when talented doctors, nurses, and midwives leave Nigeria to look for better work opportunities abroad. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h7)

question: How do most patients still pay for their medical care in Nigerian tertiary hospitals?
explanation: Since health insurance doesn't cover everyone yet, many patients unfortunately still have to pay cash right out of their pockets for drugs and hospital services. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h7)
